setting: operating units of a large knowledge-intensive services firm
research_question: What determines creative output in these units, and in particular how does the intensity of electronic performance monitoring affect creative output, through which mechanisms, and under what conditions?

variables.name: monitoring_intensity
variables.label: Intensity of electronic performance monitoring of employees in the unit (standardized index)

variables.name: creative_output
variables.label: Number and quality of novel solutions and process improvements generated by the unit, judged by an expert panel (standardized index)

variables.name: routine_output
variables.label: Volume of standard tasks completed per employee (standardized index)

variables.name: perceived_autonomy
variables.label: Employees' reported discretion over how they do their work (standardized index)

variables.name: trust_in_management
variables.label: Employees' reported trust in unit management (standardized index)

variables.name: feedback_frequency
variables.label: Frequency of performance feedback conversations between supervisors and employees (standardized index)

variables.name: feedback_quality
variables.label: Developmental quality of feedback, rated by trained observers (standardized index)

variables.name: tech_investment
variables.label: Unit spending on workplace technology and analytics (standardized index)

variables.name: wellness_program
variables.label: Scope of employee wellness programs offered by the unit (standardized index)

variables.name: job_tenure
variables.label: Average employee tenure in the unit (standardized index)

variables.name: manager_span
variables.label: Number of direct reports per supervisor (standardized index)

literature.design: Multi-level study of 310 units in a financial services firm.
literature.mechanism: Monitoring is argued to crowd out intrinsic motivation and exploratory behavior.

literature.mechanism: The authors argue that well-being frees cognitive resources for creative work.

literature.design: Natural experiment around the staggered rollout of a monitoring system in 62 call centers.
